subject: general
question: The largest nuclear power station in India is in ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tarapur**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **Tarapur Nuclear Power Plant** is located in **Tarapur**, **Maharashtra**, and is India's first commercial nuclear power station with an installed capacity of 1,000 MW, owned by the Nuclear Power Corporation of India
 
• A nuclear power plant generates electricity using nuclear energy produced by reactors, where certain unstable atomic nuclei, like uranium, undergo fission when bombarded by neutrons, releasing a large amount of energy.
 
• T**arapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS)** was launched by** Lal Bahadur Shastri’s government, **construction began in **1961**, and it was commissioned in **1969**, marking its 50th year of operation in 2019.
 
• Located in **Tarapur**, **Pune**, **Maharashtra**, it has four pressurised heavy water reactor units with a total capacity of 1,100 MW, owned by the **Maharashtra** State Electricity Distribution Company and operated by NPCIL.
 
• Power generation in Units 1 and 2 is 2×160 MW, and in Units 3 and 4, it is 2×540 MW, with a net nameplate capacity of 1280 MW, making it the second most powerful power plant in India after **Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant.**
 
• Nuclear fuel for TAPS is delivered by France, China, and Russia under IAEA safeguards, following India’s 1974 nuclear test which ended Western uranium supplies.
 
• TAPS was a collaborative effort between New Delhi and Russia, with a contract signed in 1964 and commercial operations starting in 1969, using reactors supplied by the US conglomerate General Electric.
